source.title: An Adaptive Method Stabilizing Activations for Enhanced Generalization
source.authors: Hyunseok Seung; Jaewoo Lee; Hyunsuk Ko

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Compares test accuracy of its proposed adaptive optimizer and standard adaptive optimizers with SGD on image classification benchmarks, using a different optimizer and settings from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study compares optimizers on natural-label image classification, but does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected architectures, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. ImageNet comparator values marked † are reported from prior work and are not rows. The generalization analysis is theoretical; it does not report measured generalization-gap outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own held-out accuracy comparisons between adaptive optimizers and momentum SGD on image classifiers. These directly bear on V4, although tuning includes optimizer-specific settings and is not a controlled learning-rate-only tuning comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors argue that activation-based neuronwise adaptation improves generalization over conventional adaptive baselines while approaching SGD's accuracy and adaptive methods' speed. Their ImageNet results are competitive rather than uniformly best, and comparisons there use cited baselines.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces activation-variance-based neuronwise adaptation; compares on CIFAR with 200 epochs and batch size 128, and on ImageNet with large-batch training. It does not reproduce the optimizer comparisons in the claim's cited studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported CIFAR test accuracies vary by optimizer and architecture/dataset. Figure 6 reports BN-use conditions; the text says removing BN degrades both A DA ACT and SGD but affects A DA ACT less.

fits_no_version.finding: KFAC and FOOF test accuracies compare second-order methods with other optimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Second-order preconditioning methods differ in held-out accuracy and computational cost from first-order optimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: Activation variance, effective-step-size stability, and the theoretical stability bound are analyzed; Figure 3 also varies AdaAct's preconditioning exponent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-based preconditioning choices affect activation stability and held-out accuracy.

record.peer_reviewed: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining Workshops (ICDMW); extended version states published version available at DOI 10.1109/ICDMW65004.2024.00007
record.problems: No measured training accuracy or train-test gap is reported for the optimizer comparison. CIFAR accuracy is mean and standard error across five runs; ImageNet accuracy has no uncertainty stated. ImageNet baseline values are prior-work reports rather than matched study-run comparisons. Mild tuning was performed only for Adan, FOOF, and KFAC; remaining methods use settings from [51].
record.rows_left_out: No eligible study-run V4 rows left out. ImageNet comparator values in Tables 2–3 are marked † and reported from [45], so excluded as cited prior results. Figure 7 gives trajectories without text-reported exact values; retained the text-described LeNet comparison from Figure 1 and numeric BN values from Figure 6.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting and natural-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep beyond zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.

No language benchmarks, systematic limited-versus-broad tuning comparison, Adam-to-SGD switch, or intervention isolating decoupled weight decay. The main optimizer comparisons do not establish equal or better adaptive training performance.
No batch-size comparison under a fixed epoch budget; large-batch ImageNet performance alone does not test a batch penalty.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation measure or comparison of its ranking with other generalization measures.
No memorized-example removal and retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: V4 says adaptive methods often perform worse, so AdaAct's exceptions qualify its scope rather than refute its frequency claim. CIFAR tuning is asymmetric: Adan receives learning-rate and momentum/EMA tuning, while Adam, AdamW, and SGD inherit settings; weight decay also differs across methods. Thus the results establish differences under the reported recipes, not an intrinsic optimizer ranking or a controlled test restricted to learning-rate and schedule tuning. The supplied Table 1 and Figure 7 appear inconsistent about the two middle architecture/dataset columns; preserve within-column contrasts and verify assignments rather than silently swapping values. ImageNet cited comparator values and omitted Figure 7 trajectories were already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence are not tested.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No language benchmarks; no broader tuning study, Adam-to-SGD switch, or comparison isolating decoupled weight decay.
No batch-size sweep or fixed-epoch batch-size comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or competing generalization-measure comparison.
